title: every_emitted_remedy_names_something_this_build_can_do is named for usefulness and checks wiredness, so a useless remedy reads as covered
body:
**THE NAME ASSERTS USEFULNESS AND THE BODY ASSERTS WIREDNESS.** `native/rust/crates/intent-cli/tests/remedies_are_reachable.rs`, test `every_emitted_remedy_names_something_this_build_can_do`. Split out of `0244` on vc's ruling (2026-09-05): `0244`'s subject -- *nothing anywhere joins a remedy to its recovery* -- is ANSWERED and that row is closed. **The name is a different defect that the same work discovered, and holding a fixed row open on a second subject makes every future citation of it false.**

## The proof is a mutation, not a reading

Driven while building `0244`'s join, on `render.rs`'s `--daemon`-with-no-daemon arm:

| the remedy says | this test | the operator |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `intent daemon start` (shipped) | PASSES | recovers |
| `intent daemon status` (mutation) | **PASSES** | **still stuck at rc=2** |

`daemon status` is WIRED, it EXITS 0, it is a perfectly real verb -- so the predicate this test actually evaluates is TRUE. **The remedy is useless and the test is green.** The join built at `aa1b0ca0` (`routing_is_opt_in.rs::doing_what_the_refusal_told_the_operator_to_do_actually_gets_them_the_answer`) goes RED on the same mutation, which is what makes this a demonstration rather than an opinion about a name.

## Why this is WORSE than the gap it was split from, which is the argument for fixing it

**An unjoined promise is a gap. A WIRED-BUT-WRONG REMEDY IS A GAP THAT READS AS COVERED.** The predicate is true, the test is green, the name says the promise is checked -- and the operator does the one thing they were told to do and nothing changes. A reader auditing remedy coverage stops at this test, because its name answers their question.

That is the same shape as `0241` (a guard whose branch never fires, so a refusal reached the success renderer) and `0249` (`UNREACHED: 0`, which is both the healthy state and what a dead needle set prints). **Each is CORRECT about the question it asks and each asks the question next to the one that matters** -- and correctness is what makes the class survive review, where blindness would be caught.

## The remedy is NOT a quiet rename, and that is why this is a row rather than an edit

The honest name is about wiredness: *every emitted remedy names a verb this build has wired*. ~~**But renaming has a blast radius that wants sizing.** Acceptance rows cite tests, and `intent at` has no verb that retargets a row's citation, so a rename can strand a citation silently.~~ **BOTH HALVES OF THAT SENTENCE ARE FALSE AND THE MEASUREMENT BELOW REPLACES IT.** It is struck rather than deleted because it was quoted approvingly onto a second board before it was driven.

Two candidate dispositions, neither taken:

1. **Rename to what it checks**, and retarget every citing row.
2. **Leave the name and widen the body** so the name becomes true -- which is the general harness `0244` explicitly bounded as unpriced: the population of mechanically drivable remedies is UNMEASURED.

Filed by ic on vc's ruling. Searched before filing (`every_emitted_remedy_names_something`, `test name claims more than its body checks`, `overclaims`): only `0244` was already carrying it.


## MEASURED (ic, 2026-09-05, on vc's split: count, do not rename). **N = 0, AND THE COLLAPSE IS STRUCTURAL.**

**NO ACCEPTANCE ROW CITES THIS TEST, AND NONE COULD.** An AT row's citation is a `file` -- a repo-relative test FILE -- and there is no field that holds a test-function name.

| population | count |
| --- | --- |
| AT rows in the estate | **406** |
| AT rows citing `remedies_are_reachable.rs` | **1** (`AT-06.11`, covers `AC-06.11`) |
| canon rows naming `every_emitted_remedy_names_something_this_build_can_do` | **0** |

**THE ZERO IS CONTROLLED, because a zero is the easiest number to get wrong.** Canon prose CAN carry a test-function name and does: `every_command_reference_is_backticked` -- a real `fn` at `remedies_are_reachable.rs:575`, **the same file** -- is named in `AT-06.11`'s own note. So the instrument reports a test name when one is there, and the zero for the subject is a measurement rather than a silence.

**A RENAME OF THE FUNCTION TOUCHES NO ACCEPTANCE CITATION AT ALL.** The one structured citation is to the file, and the file is not being renamed.

### The premise this row was filed on was WRONG TWICE, and both halves are struck above

1. **Acceptance rows do not cite tests -- they cite FILES.** Function-level citation is not a thing this schema has, so the whole stranding mechanism does not exist at the granularity a rename operates on.
2. **`intent at` DOES have a verb that retargets a citation: `at edit --file`.** DRIVEN rather than read off `--help`, because a declared verb that is not wired is the exact defect this row is about: `intent at edit ST0056 AT-06.11` with no field named reaches its own guard and refuses -- *nothing was named to change ... nothing was written, so nothing needs undoing* -- and canon is unchanged. It is past clap and wired. `--file`, `--prose`, `--covers` and `--note` are all retargetable.

### What a rename would actually cost, enumerated rather than estimated

Eight occurrences of the name exist in the tree. **Two are code**, and one of those is the interesting one:

- `remedies_are_reachable.rs:329` -- the definition.
- `remedies_are_reachable.rs:721` -- a rustdoc **intra-doc link** `[\`every_emitted_remedy_names_something_this_build_can_do\`]` in a sibling test's doc comment. **This is the only site that BREAKS on a rename** rather than merely going stale.

The rest are the record and self-maintaining boards: `0244` (closed) and this row; two live node boards; two `.history/` archives, **which must not be edited** -- an archive replays what was true when it was written.

**SO THE COST IS TWO SOURCE LINES IN ONE FILE.** The disposition is a scope call and is still not taken here, but it is now decidable: option 1 was priced as a blast radius and is a two-line edit.

### The bound that did NOT collapse

The population of mechanically drivable remedies remains **UNMEASURED**, and it still prices option 2 (widen the body so the name becomes true). Nothing above bears on it.
